title: The stabilizer of an O_E-lattice is open
statement: Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $E$-vector space with its $\ell$-adic topology (the product topology for any $E$-basis), and let $\Lambda_0\subset V$ be a finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-submodule spanning $V$ over $E$. Then the subgroup $\{u\in\operatorname{GL}_E(V):u(\Lambda_0)=\Lambda_0\}$ is open in $\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$ for the topology induced by the compact-open topology on continuous linear maps $V\to V$.

source.place: Stanford Weil II seminar, lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 2: GL(Lambda_0) is an open subgroup of GL_n(E)

proof.text: The valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ is a discrete valuation ring by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The submodule $\Lambda_0$ is torsion-free because it lies in the $E$-vector space $V$, and it is finitely generated by hypothesis. The Mathlib leaf [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] therefore makes $\Lambda_0$ finite free over $\mathcal O_E$. Since it spans $V$, its rank is $\dim_E V$; choose an $\mathcal O_E$-basis $(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$ of $\Lambda_0$, which is also an $E$-basis of $V$.

source.place: Lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 2 (choose a lattice basis)

proof.text: Write elements of $\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$ as matrices in the basis $(e_j)$. Since $(e_j)$ is an $\mathcal O_E$-basis of $\Lambda_0$, $u(\Lambda_0)\subseteq\Lambda_0$ iff all entries of the matrix $A$ of $u$ lie in $\mathcal O_E$, so the stabilizer is exactly the set of $A$ such that $A$ and $A^{-1}$ have entries in $\mathcal O_E$, i.e. $\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$. For any such $A$ and any $B\in M_n(\mathfrak m_E)$, $A+B$ has entries in $\mathcal O_E$; writing $A+B=A(I+A^{-1}B)$, the matrix $A^{-1}B$ has entries in $\mathfrak m_E$, so $\det(I+A^{-1}B)\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak m_E}$ is a unit of the local ring $\mathcal O_E$ and $I+A^{-1}B$ is invertible over $\mathcal O_E$ (adjugate formula). Hence $A+M_n(\mathfrak m_E)\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_n(\mathcal O_E)$.

source.place: Lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 2 (GL(\Lambda_0) is open in GL_n(E))

proof.text: For each pair $(i,j)$ the entry map $u\mapsto u_{ij}$ (the $i$-th coordinate of $u(e_j)$) is continuous on $\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$ for the compact-open topology: evaluation at the point $e_j$ is continuous for the compact-open topology (a point is compact), and the coordinate functions are continuous for the product topology on $V$. The set $\mathfrak m_E=\{x:|x|_E<1\}$ is open in $E$ because $|\cdot|_E$ is continuous. So $\{u:u_{ij}-A_{ij}\in\mathfrak m_E\text{ for all }i,j\}$, i.e. $A+M_n(\mathfrak m_E)$, is a finite intersection of preimages of open sets, hence open in $\operatorname{GL}_E(V)$; by the previous step it contains $A$ and lies in the stabilizer. Thus the stabilizer is a neighborhood of each of its points, hence open.

proof_origin.place: Lecture 19, Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 2; the matrix-neighborhood details are written out here
